T-PAT-8.statusReason: The Ngogo patrol record has no observation effort, so months without a patrol are mostly months nobody observed. Ruling of 2026-09-29: not scorable; no sim-vs-real verdict is given.
T-PAT-8.rule: §5.3.1 P5: Spearman ρ between monthly patrol rate (Dryad kk33f patrol dates) and monthly fruit availability (the Potts et al. 2020 site series, ripe fruit score), bootstrap 90% CI over months; band = that CI.

frozenTarget.basis: bootstrap 90% CI over months (docs/realism-design.md §5.3.1 P5 rule), computed before any run of the corrected model

independent.method: percentile bootstrap, months resampled with replacement; Spearman ρ on average ranks

agreement.note: Same 211 months and 279 patrols. ρ 0.064 (counts) vs frozen 0.0591 (per 30 days): the only difference is the rate definition, since dividing by month length reorders tied counts (per-30-day ρ here 0.059). Band edges differ by that and by bootstrap noise (10000 vs 4000 replicates, different seeds).

T-BRD-1.status: held out; the share is partly encoded
T-BRD-1.rule: §5.3.1 P5: the share of border stops followed by an advance toward the rivals, and its slope on the number of males present. The male-count slope is the non-circular part; the share is partly encoded through patrolIncursionP.
T-BRD-1.unsupported: S3 Data do not count males: "adult party size" counts all adults of both sexes within visibility (Lemoine et al. 2023 methods). The male-count slope cannot be computed; the slope on adults present is the logged substitute (realism-design.md §5.3.1 implementation notes), and the sim must count adults the same way.

frozenTarget.basis: cluster-bootstrap 90% CI (docs/realism-design.md §5.3.1 P5 rule), computed before any run of the corrected model; the share part (band 0.411-0.486) is partly encoded through patrolIncursionP (fitted to T-PAT-6) and is reported, not scored

independent.method: logistic regression (Newton–Raphson) of approach rivals (0/1) on adult party size; percentile 90% cluster bootstrap over group-days (dates nested in groups, as the article models them)

agreement.note: Same 625 stops and 283 group-days. Share 0.448 and slope 0.072 match the frozen values; the interval edges differ only by bootstrap noise (10000 vs 4000 replicates, different seeds).

T-BRD-1.dataNotes: 58 of 625 rows have 'time spent' under 5 min although the article selects stops of ≥ 5 min; the column may measure something else, so no row is dropped. 304 hill stops, 321 low-place stops.

band.basis: cluster-bootstrap 90% CI (docs/realism-design.md §5.3.1 P5 rule), computed before any run of the corrected model; the share part (band 0.411-0.486) is partly encoded through patrolIncursionP (fitted to T-PAT-6) and is reported, not scored

check.label: Patrol sector concentration
check.note: Encoded-descriptive check (Amendment A was chosen after reading this pattern): reported, never counted as validation. Real pattern: repeat patrols on contested edges and months of neglect elsewhere (Watts & Mitani 2001: one sector patrolled 20 times in 11 months, another 158 days without a patrol).

band.basis: pattern (Amendment A); encoded-descriptive check, never counted as validation

compromised.note: Patrol predictors: compromised this cycle (P1 changed its predictor after its value was seen). Reported, never counted, nothing tuned against it.

preFission.source: Dryad kk33f (observed patrols; effort varies by year)

seasonality.note: Ngogo patrols by calendar month mix behaviour with the observers' field seasons (43% fall in June–July); Gombe patrols come from year-round daily focal follows.

real.source: Mitani, Watts & Amsler 2010 (Curr Biol); areas from Langergraber et al. 2017

labels: partially encoded (scored against the paired baseline)
expansion.rule: field-scenario.ts expansion: West gets 6 extra adult males; its 95% range area change from year 1 to year 10, relative to the same seed's baseline, counted only after lethal wins; the centre must shift toward the neighbours.

notComparable: Patrol routes: no open patrol tracks exist for any site, so route shape, speed and where patrols turn back cannot be compared.
T-PAT-8 (patrols vs fruit): the Ngogo record has no observation effort; months without a patrol are mostly unobserved.
The male-count slope of T-BRD-1: the Taï data count adults of both sexes, not males.
Female participation at Ngogo and patrol distance anywhere: only published summaries exist, no open records.
Incursion depth and the location of killings: published as maps only (not copied) or as single numbers.

privacy: Derived statistics only: counts, shares, rates, rank correlations, slopes and distances in range radii. No coordinates, no dates finer than a month, no individual names.
